breakdown.description: The prompt sets the free-end rotation to zero, even though a cantilever’s free end is generally free to rotate under an end point load.
breakdown.reason: The generated specification correctly applies physically accurate cantilever boundary conditions: fixed end at x=0 has v(0)=0 and θ(0)=0, while the free end at x=L has M(L)=0. It explicitly computes a non-zero free-end rotation θ(L) = 0.001152 rad, directly contradicting the flawed instruction to set free-end rotation to zero.

breakdown.description: The prompt treats the bending moment as constant and equal to P L over the entire span, even though the cantilever moment varies linearly from the free end to the fixed end.
breakdown.reason: The generated specification uses the standard cantilever tip-load formulas θ(L) = PL²/(2EI) and v(L) = PL³/(3EI), which are derived from the linearly varying bending moment distribution M(x) = P(L−x). It does not treat the moment as constant equal to PL over the full span, correctly resolving this inconsistency.
